Dismissive of preventative care - Lacks true avian expertise and leaves first-time bird owners blind.   ​I brought my young Green Cheek Conure, Sparrow, here in April for an initial new-pet wellness check and to have his leg band removed. If you are looking for proactive, diagnostic avian medicine, look elsewhere.
​As a first-time bird owner, I came to this clinic expecting medical guidance from a hospital that advertises care for birds. Instead, the visit consisted of bare-minimum husbandry advice anyone could find on a basic pet website.
​The most damaging failure was their complete dismissal of preventative health and diagnostic testing. When I explicitly asked about vaccines and how to test for latent illnesses or carrier diseases, the staff simply brushed me off, saying "we don't give birds shots like dogs or cats." While companion parrots do not receive routine annual injections, any competent clinic seeing avian patients has a duty to explain what real avian preventative medicine actually looks like: baseline complete blood counts (CBC), choanal/cloacal Gram stains, and PCR screening panels for common pet-trade pathogens. Even worse, because they are general practitioners and not board-certified avian specialists, they should have informed me of their diagnostic limitations and referred me to an avian specialist who could properly screen him.
​Instead of educating a new owner on how birds mask illness or offering baseline testing, they sent us out the door with zero diagnostic insight. Six months later, Sparrow passed away from a severe, localized nasal bacterial infection and airway blockage. Having general medical transparency, baseline disease testing, or a referral to a specialist back in April could have caught underlying health risks, established a medical baseline, or educated us on warning signs when we still had time to act. Instead, we were left completely in the dark until a critical emergency occurred six months down the line when it was already too late.
​On top of that, while they cut off his open split-ring band ("A 1249"), they never bothered to explain what that hardware actually meant: an untraceable commercial broker inventory tag rather than a legitimate closed breeder band. They missed a crucial opportunity to educate a client on the biological hazards common to high-volume commercial supply chains.
​A general practice that treats exotic pets as a sideline and brushes off preventative testing is a liability to your animal. If you have a bird, skip this clinic and find a dedicated, board-certified avian specialist who will actually run diagnostics and protect your pet's life before an emergency happens. RIP - "Sparrow" ❤️

Took our 22 year old cockatiel in today for respiratory issues. Amazing staff and the doctor was exceptional!!! We were early and she took us back immediately. Made our boy all better. Highly recommend for bird care! Plus Rosie the African Grey was an added bonus.

Y'all need a new front desk lady. Peggy is rude, doesn't answer questions, and will hang up on you if you ask any questions she doesn't know the answer to.
I don't know how their service is, because this lady didn't wanna do her job.
People here are very kind n helpful thank you!

We brought our husky Blue here for his neuter, and the care from Dr. Powers and her team was truly exceptional. The day after surgery we noticed some bleeding and were really worried. Even though it was her day off, Dr. Powers still came in with her staff just to check on him. She examined him carefully, reassured us, and was kind enough to wash him up and make sure his incisions looked clean and healthy.

That level of compassion and dedication meant so much to us. They treated our boy like their own and made us feel completely at ease. We genuinely appreciate Dr. Powers and her team, and we highly recommend this hospital to anyone looking for real, attentive care.
Thank you for taking care of Riley our parrot 🦜 fast service awesome 👏🏼 …
Great experience with my guinea pigs, very helpful and kind staff, a little concerned about med dosage but gave me accurate care info to go with then, and was also very affordable

This was a horrible vet experience, not only did the vet not give me any helpful information but she had to read off of the papers she gave me because she was hesitating on care questions. The vet tech was also very rude, they both stressed my snake out so much from the way they were handling him, they also gave me contradictory information on temperature and humidity. And the care guides they provided were outdated and had false information.

I brought my cat here after taking him to an emergency vet on the advice of an office admin here.

They were incredibly professional and kind throughout my entire time interacting with the staff.

Unfortunately my cat did not survive his illness and I cannot overstate how nice and accommodating the staff was. Dr. Powers in particular I remember but the vet technicians were also very nice to me and my cat.

I know they did everything they could and I would recommend this office to any pet owner.
Rocky couldn't wait to get his nails and beak done!

Just called to see if they can see my guinea pig and they told me no, but on the website it says they do see pocket animals. Also, the person who answered the phone was rude. Was going to be the first time I take my guinea pig there but looks like no business from me.

Friendly and professional. They take care of our cars Toast and Tofu exceptionally well. Tofu is a Persian and gets matted every year. The vets are patient and kind with my Tofu’s difficult matting. Toast is a butthead with them, but he’s an orange cat so I don’t expect any better.
Excellent. We've been to them before to care for our cats. Caring, knowledgeable and efficient. I  highly recommend.  BRYN

Amazing!  I have taken both of my ferrets here, and this place is friendly, clean, amazing doctors that talk with you to get a very good understanding of the little guys to give them the best treatment.  And I think that the price is great too, having exotic pets is pricey obviously, but even surgery for one of my boys didn’t break the bank.  And even if you have questions after a visit they are more than helpful over the phone.  I drive 17 miles one way just to go to this clinic!!!  It’s amazing!  Oh, and I’m not sure if this is just my own experience but they seem to be able to schedule appointments quick!  All in all, this place is great, if you have ferrets and can make the drive, I stand by this place with my soul!
Dr was amazing with my bird and her assistant was so helpful and Yenefer was so kind and explained everything Great service all employees were kind they took me in fast !
My dog has itchy butt and they helped his itchy butt not be itchy butt.

I rate Dr. Powers a 1/5 because I took my Indonesian Blue Tongue Skink in for reptile mites which are quite common in reptiles.  She didn’t really handle him too much, and didn’t seem to know much about his kind.  She lied to me telling me that the medicine she advised and applied to him(Advantage II) was “prescription” only.  FALSE.  I’m aware that i can purchase that very medication over the counter at any local PetsMart or Petco as it is used on kittens and cats.  I asked her how much it was since I can get one dose for $16.99, she then told me that it was $28.  So overall, i feel lied to, and cheated and my poor reptile wasn’t treated the way he should have been since she misrepresented herself.  Not to mention, the questions she was asking me were quite offensive, almost felt like an interrogation as if i don’t have all of my pets’ best interest in heart and mind.  I  have since taken him to a different well trusted true exotic vet since he still had mites after his visit with her on Monday(12/2/24).

You should stick to warm blooded animals, this way you don’t overpromise and under deliver. Thank you but no thank you.

A big fat zero is what it should be. Took my 5 week old cockatiel to a different vet before this one. Last vet check on bird...swabbed his crop, listen to his lungs, said we should make sure he eats and said we should come back after the weekend. We needed more answers and wanted a second opinion. Came to this VET and she did absolutely nothing with my bird! Didn't even touch him. Said he looks terrible his 3 different meds you can go pick up and fed him and that's it. Did not even touch the bird and now he's dead! After those medicine were giving my bird became very tired, didn't want to move, called and asked about it. Was told he probably won't live then and that was that. WHAT WAS THE POINT OF ANOTHER OPINION WHEN THIS VET REFUSED TO EVEN TOUCH MY BIRD! Accused me of not knowing how to take care of baby birds when I just in fact raised a cockatiel before this one that is currently 6 months old and I had no issues with him. My point, take care of your patients and actually look, and listen to the poor animals and not assume the human is neglecting the poor animal. Spent hundreds of dollars here to be treated like I did something wrong when this is the 2nd one I came to because I was so worried and they basically killed my bird. Thanks so not much!

This clinic is amazing not only did they help me out with the bill out of the kindness of their heart? They were also compassionate and caring with my cat. I will definitely continue to visit this clinic as long as I can until they run me off.

I had the heartbreaking experience of an attack on my chickens, losing 6 of my 7 girls. My lone survivor, Rose, was badly injured. I found Ten West Bird & Animal Hospital online, and called and was able to get an appointment/be seen within …
They are very sweet. i don't want to ding them on a particular thing. I will just remind them that if they quote you a price please keep your word. I understand if other things need to be done.
Caring and compassionate!
